facts.statement: The genus Microsuchus was described by De Saez in 1928.
Microsuchus is classified as an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylians within the group Notosuchia.
facts.quote: Microsuchus is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylians, belonging to Notosuchia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Microsuchus have been found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation from the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, dating to the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Microsuchus was originally classified as a goniopholidid but was later redescribed as either a neosuchian or notosuchian.
facts.quote: Originally classified as a goniopholidid on the basis of the platycoelous vertebral centra, Microsuchus was recently redescribed and recovered as either a neosuchian or notosuchian.

facts.statement: A 2017 cladistic analysis recovered Microsuchus as a primitive notosuchian.
facts.quote: A 2017 cladistic analysis of Razanandrongobe further clarified the phylogenetic position of Microsuchus by recovering it as a primitive notosuchian.

facts.statement: Microsuchus is characterized by a bulge near the second sacral vertebra, elongated rear limb bones, and triangular tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Diagnostic features include the presence of a bulge lateral to the prezygapophyses of the second sacral vertebra, elongated posterior zeugopodia, and proximal caudal centra with a triangular cross section.

facts.statement: Microsuchus lived approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)
